extracted.intended_audience: Authors (and reviewers/ACs) submitting papers to EACL 2023
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and review criteria for addressing ethical issues in papers submitted to the EACL 2023 main conference (including dataset, application, identity, and compute-related ethical considerations) and for reviewer/committee handling of flagged ethical concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor ACL Code of Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are required to honor the ethical code set out in the ACL Code of Ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your work is conformant to the ACL Code of Ethics. Where a paper may raise ethical issues, include an explicit discussion of these issues; the ethics committee reserves the right to reject papers on ethical grounds or if authors have inadequately addressed legitimate ethical concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ACM Code of Ethics / legal and ethical compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers may be rejected on the basis of ethical or legal concerns; ensure compliance with the ACM Code of Ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check both ethical and legal constraints (e.g., intellectual property, privacy). Recommendations for reject/accept on ethical grounds come from the ethics committee with input from initial reviewers, but final accept/reject decisions remain with the Program Chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include an explicit ethical considerations section
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should have an 'ethical considerations' section in their paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extra space is provided after the 8th page (4th page for short papers) for an ethics/broader impact statement; place this after the conclusion so the main paper still fits the page limit. Papers that report research raising ethical issues but do not discuss such issues are likely to be rejected on ethical grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibility to consider and flag ethics concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: EACL reviewers are asked to consider the points listed in the ethics review questions and indicate whether a paper should be flagged for further ethics review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should explain what considerations lead them to recommend flagging; flagged papers are then examined by the dedicated ethics reviewing committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics committee review process and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: A dedicated reviewing committee will review papers flagged as problematic and recommend whether to accept as is, reject on ethical grounds, or conditionally accept with specified required changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditional accepts will be re-reviewed by the ethics committee at camera-ready to determine whether concerns have been adequately addressed. The ethics committee is available to respond to authors' questions about feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset: comply with sources' terms of use, IP, and privacy rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that your dataset has been collected in a manner consistent with the terms of use of any sources and with intellectual property and privacy rights of original authors of the texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fact that a dataset has been previously used does not necessarily make it acceptable. If appropriate, check that informed consent was signed. Consult your institution's data officer or review board for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset: detail collection process and annotator compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail the dataset collection process and conditions; if manual work was involved, describe measures taken to ensure crowd workers or other annotators were fairly compensated and how fair compensation was determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough information so reviewers can assess fairness and labor practices; describe steps taken to recruit, train, and compensate annotators and how compensation was decided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset: indicate IRB approval where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Please indicate if your project was approved by an IRB (institutional review board).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relevant, state IRB approval and provide appropriate documentation or explanation. (Page cites APA link for discussion of IRBs in US context.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset: describe dataset characteristics and populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the characteristics of the dataset in enough detail for a reader to understand which speaker populations the technology could be expected to work for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For suggestions of what to include, see cited resources (Bender and Friedman 2018; Mitchell et al. 2019; Gebru et al. 2018). Provide demographic/representation information and domain coverage so limitations and expected generalization are clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset: mitigate risks from dataset quality issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the steps taken to ensure that potential problems with the quality of the dataset do not create additional risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain quality-control procedures, cleaning, validation, and any limitations that might affect downstream harms; describe how poor quality was detected and mitigated.

rubrics_metrics.name: NLP application: alignment between task and deployment use case
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure there is good alignment between the task carried out automatically and the intended real-world use case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully consider how the technology could be deployed in actual use cases and whether the automated task matches the use case requirements and constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: NLP application: state intended use and stakeholders (beneficiaries and harms)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the technology is functioning as intended, who benefits? Who might be harmed, and how?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly identify beneficiaries and those potentially harmed; discuss how benefits/harms arise from intended deployments.

rubrics_metrics.name: NLP application: analyze failure modes and their harms
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the failure modes, and in case of failure, who might be harmed and how?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe plausible failures, their likelihood/severity, and concrete impacts on users or third parties; include mitigation strategies if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: NLP application: analyze biases in dataset and model
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the biases included in the dataset and trained model, and how might they contribute to failure modes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document known biases, their sources, and anticipated effects; cite relevant literature on bias in NLP (e.g., Blodgett et al. 2020) and explain how biases affect performance and harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: NLP application: assess misuse potential and mitigations
rubrics_metrics.description: What kinds of potential misuse is there for the technology and what harms might ensue? What could be done to prevent such misuse/what should regulators know about this technology?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider adversarial or unintended uses; propose technical, policy, or deployment controls to limit misuse and inform stakeholders/regulators.

rubrics_metrics.name: NLP application: evaluate risks if system learns from user input
rubrics_metrics.description: If the system as deployed would learn from further user input, what further risks of harm might ensue and how can these be mitigated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss feedback-loop risks, data contamination, privacy exposures, and measures like filtering, human review, or safe-update procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: NLP application: consider disproportionate harm to vulnerable populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Are any of the possible harms you've identified likely to fall disproportionately on populations that already experience marginalization or are otherwise vulnerable?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify at-risk groups, assess likelihood and severity of disproportionate impacts, and describe steps taken to reduce such disparities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic/identity: avoid attributing or essentializing identity characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid attributing (assigning without asking) identity characteristics to people whose language is studied or essentializing identity characteristics (suggesting people speak/write a certain way because of their demographics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, use self-identified characteristics; if not possible, acknowledge limitations and avoid overgeneralization. Consider reframing the research question to avoid attributing identity where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic/identity: motivate categories and discuss ethical implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Motivate the range of values used for identity characteristics in terms of how they relate to the research question and discuss the ethical implications of categorizing people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why chosen demographic categories are relevant, how they were obtained, and reflect on harms/limitations of categorization; for gender-specific discussion see Larson 2017.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult IRB or equivalent on working with human-subject data
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to consult with their institutional review boards (IRB) or equivalent for input on working with data from human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use institutional resources for guidance on consent, anonymization, data retention, and other human-subjects protections; indicate consultations or determinations in the ethics section where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute/energy: report and minimize energy/carbon costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the energy resources expended on research; estimate energy/carbon costs of experiments and model deployment context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tools such as Henderson et al.'s experiment impact tracker or proxies like computing platform and running time when precise estimates are infeasible. Discuss steps taken or possible to reduce carbon costs and trade-offs with accuracy/performance (cite Strubell et al. 2019).
